To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a new method to control the CSTR network, which is based on thermodynamic principles.

(i) the Brayton-Mosser formulation can be used for any chemical reaction kinetics, (ii) the closed loop energy can be shaped to be equal (up to an arbitrary small positive constant) to the thermal part availability with the heat flux as the only control, and (iii) this is achieved using the same potential function as for the open loop system.
we propose a novel approach for stabilizing CSTR networks based on a thermodynamic stability criterion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of stabilizing feedback laws for nonlinear control systems based on the passivity properties of their energy storage elements.
the design of stabilizing controllers for the Port based models of CSTR networks using the BraytonMoser formulation.
the stabilization of the CSTR networks by means of thermodynamic based storage functions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Brayton-Mosser formulation is the most appropriate for the CSTR modeling in terms of energy shaping and that it can be applied to any reaction kinetics.

the Brayton-Mosser formulation of the CSTR model with the extended IDA-Passivity Based Controller approach provides a systematic way of controlling the CSTR model in a thermodynamically stable way, without the need to know the chemical reaction kinetics, and without the need to impose any restrictions on the reaction kinetics.

the Brayton-Mosser formulation of the CSTR model is thermodynamically consistent and the IDA-PBC approach allows the design of a stabilizing feedback controller without any restriction on chemical reaction kinetics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the thermodynamic stability criteria are sufficient conditions for the existence of an energy shaping storage function.
the Brayton-Mosher formulation can be used for any reaction kinetics without any restriction on its stability.
the thermodynamic stability criteria of a system is a necessary and sufficient condition for its stabilizability by a storage function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Brayton-Mosser model of a CSTR can be stabilized with any potential function satisfying the thermodynamic stability conditions.
the Brayton-Mossers formulation of the non isothermic CSTR is thermodynamic consistent, which opens up the possibility to use thermodynamic stability criteria for the control of CSTR networks.
the Brayton-Mooser formulation can be used to design a control strategy for the CSTR model without any knowledge of the reaction kinetics.
